questions.q: Aqueous sodium hydroxide is added to a solution. A white precipitate forms that dissolves in excess, giving a colourless solution. Which ion is present?
questions.why: Zn²⁺ gives a white ppt. soluble in excess; the Ca²⁺ white ppt. is insoluble in excess.
ZnO reacts with both acids and bases to give a salt and water; CaO and CuO are basic, SO₂ is acidic.

questions.q: Which test shows that a solution contains sulfate ions?
options: acidify with dilute nitric acid, add aqueous silver nitrate: white ppt.
acidify with dilute sulfuric acid, add aqueous barium nitrate: white ppt.
acidify with dilute nitric acid, add aqueous barium nitrate: white ppt.
questions.why: Sulfuric acid would add sulfate ions itself; silver nitrate is the test for halides.

questions.q: Copper(II) sulfate crystals are made from dilute sulfuric acid and excess copper(II) oxide. Why is excess copper(II) oxide used, and how is the excess removed?
questions.model: To make sure all the acid has reacted (so the salt is not contaminated with acid); the excess solid is removed by filtration.
points: all the acid used up / reacts
